body:
RECONNAISSANCE DONE BY THE CHIEF: BOTH OSF DEPOSITS ARE REACHABLE FROM THIS ENVIRONMENT. Nobody
had checked whether the inspection was even possible, and it would have been an unpleasant thing
to discover after assigning it.

  https://osf.io/gptkz/   HTTP 200   (Ost 2022 serial reproduction -- War of the Ghosts)
  https://osf.io/h2pkv/   HTTP 200   (NFRD)
  api.github.com/repos/phoebsc/Naturalistic-Free-Recall-Dataset   HTTP 200
  api.osf.io/v2/nodes/...  HTTP 401 -- "Authentication credentials were not provided"

SO: the public node pages and GitHub are open; the OSF v2 REST API wants a token. That is a
route problem, not an access problem -- the deposits are public, the machine-readable API is what
is gated. Work the public file listing and the GitHub repository first, and only ask the owner
for an OSF token if the file listing genuinely cannot be obtained without one.

bd-01M17JFDHKHPD6N6JWA7NCMM4A IS YOURS, root, and it JUMPS AHEAD OF THE NFRD INVENTORY you are
already holding. Not because NFRD is less good -- on paper it is the better corpus -- but because
gptkz is War of the Ghosts, and WarOfTheGhostsModel is a validated NarrativeGraph and
NarrativeHierarchy that this project has spent its entire life tuning against. Every other corpus
needs a source representation built from nothing before a single number exists. This one needs
the recall side and the source side is already sitting in fixtures.

THE ONE QUESTION THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING, and I want it answered before anything else is
reported: DOES THE DEPOSIT CONTAIN THE RAW WRITTEN REPRODUCTIONS, or only coded words, details,
themes and analysis tables? Corpus or spreadsheet. Everything else is secondary and I would
rather have that one answer in ten minutes than a complete inventory in an hour.

THEN, in order:
  2. Does their War of the Ghosts source text match OURS? Bartlett's text has variants. A
     different variant means our NarrativeGraph does not describe their stimulus and the whole
     advantage evaporates -- so check this early, not last.
  3. Licence and redistribution terms.
  4. Chain and generation identifiers intact, so a five-generation trajectory can be reconstructed
     per chain rather than a bag of 80 texts.
  5. Verbatim participant text or edited? Same observation-versus-derivation classification I
     required for NFRD.

MY AMENDED GATE APPLIES: if the licence is open, fetch and inspect freely, no owner sign-off. I
over-gated CC0 data earlier today and have narrowed it. Record provenance and licence per file,
and keep participant text out of the repository proper until you have reported -- docs/ for
findings, not a data drop.

If the raw texts are there and the source variant matches, that is the first real measurement
this project has ever been in a position to make.
